### MEDIUM: Persisted cache\-routing holders and demand add an account\-scoped store not covered by the threat model
[CHANGELOG\.md:394](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/29f85d1c5c47ef696fc0cd88ce2c83a7a3ce6f08/CHANGELOG.md#L394) · T-041, T-059

The changelog describes a write\-behind Postgres copy of SSD cache holders and observed demand that survives coordinator restarts\. T\-041 only covers provider\-side at\-rest artifacts and in\-memory routing scope\. T\-059 does not mention this new store\. The rows carry account\-derived scope HMACs, model builds, prefix\-length and timing data, so they may expose which accounts reused prefixes after a database compromise or admin export\. They may also survive account erasure\. Fix: add this store to T\-041/T\-059\. Confirm it contains no raw prompts, chain hashes or account IDs\. Include it in the account\-erasure inventory\. Test that rows are purged on erasure and that the cache\-key generation can rotate\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: New per\-account hardware\-interest table with admin email export is outside the erasure and admin\-export model
[CHANGELOG\.md:309](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/29f85d1c5c47ef696fc0cd88ce2c83a7a3ce6f08/CHANGELOG.md#L309) · T-059

The changelog adds durable Earn\-page notification interest stored per authenticated account, plus a bounded admin\-only export joined to current email\. This is a new PII\-linked table and export path\. T\-059 does not list it among the data an account erasure must remove, and TB\-006 does not list the export among admin\-surface exports\. An erased account could leave its email\-linked interest rows behind or still appear in exports\. Fix: add the table and export to T\-059 and TB\-006\. Delete or anonymize rows on erasure\. Add a regression test and audit logging for the export\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Changelog describes SSD prefix\-cache policy changes that T\-041's sign\-off does not cover
[CHANGELOG\.md:1062](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/29f85d1c5c47ef696fc0cd88ce2c83a7a3ce6f08/CHANGELOG.md#L1062) · A-001, T-041

CHANGELOG\.md lines 1060\-1062 state that the default shared SSD cache ceiling is now 100 GiB \(half of available space\) and that complete dense Qwen prefix checkpoints are stored on encrypted SSD by default\. These checkpoints include attention KV and recurrent state, and the codec is extended to Qwen MoE\. T\-041, including its detection\_hint, still records a budget of available\-disk/2 with no fixed ceiling\. Its per\-donation adoption\-bound and benefit\-floor gate and its DBK3 block format were signed off for attention\-KV blocks only\. A new at\-rest artifact class \(whole\-prefix checkpoints with recurrent state\) is enabled by default on provider disks\. Its filename and metadata derivation, TTL, salt scoping and cross\-account isolation are not re\-reviewed in the threat model, and the stated ceiling now contradicts it\. Only changelog prose is visible here, not the provider code, so this is a documentation and sign\-off gap rather than a confirmed code regression\. Fix: update T\-041 and its detection\_hint to state the checkpoint format, the actual disk\-ceiling policy and the gating\. Confirm that checkpoint names and metadata use only HMAC tags, that salt scoping is preserved, and that the 30\-minute TTL applies\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### MEDIUM: Peer\-reported KV rate drives other providers' cold admission and autopilot fit, keyed only on self\-reported identifiers
[coordinator/registry/cold\_kv\_estimate\.go:145](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/29f85d1c5c47ef696fc0cd88ce2c83a7a3ce6f08/coordinator/registry/cold_kv_estimate.go#L145) · ADV-001, T-007, T-027, TB-002

observedColdKVRateLocked takes KVBytesPerToken from any routing\-eligible peer's self\-reported capacity slot\. coldKVEstimatesLocked then takes the MAX across peers and applies it as the cold\-model KV estimate for every other provider with the same key \(model, WeightHash, version, metallib\)\. WeightHash and PromptWorkIdentity\.ModelArtifactHash are provider\-supplied, and weight\-hash enforcement is fail\-open \(TB\-002/SEC\-007\)\. A malicious but eligible provider can therefore advertise a loaded slot with an inflated rate up to kvbudget\.MaxBytesPerToken, after copying a competitor's artifact hash\. Competitors' cold KV budget in MemoryAdmits and autopilot ColdTokenBudget is then overstated, so they are wrongly rejected for larger requests or lose autopilot fit and routing share\. A single peer with an unrealistically low rate can instead create an under\-estimate, since only >0 is checked, with no lower bound or plausibility check against model/hardware\. The under\-estimate over\-admits or mis\-plans loads\. Destination gates remain authoritative, so impact is bounded to routing/availability manipulation\. Fix: do not accept a peer rate from a single provider\. Require corroboration from several distinct accounts or machines, or derive the rate from catalog/structural model metadata\. Clamp to a plausible range for the model, and use a median or quorum instead of the max\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### LOW: Public capacity snapshot now runs provider\-fed cold\-KV forecast while holding the registry read lock
[coordinator/registry/model\_capacity\.go:84](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/29f85d1c5c47ef696fc0cd88ce2c83a7a3ce6f08/coordinator/registry/model_capacity.go#L84) · new attack surface

ModelCapacitySnapshot now calls r\.coldKVEstimatesLocked\(providers, "", now\) inside the long r\.mu\.RLock section, then takes every p\.mu in the same loop\. The sibling fleet\_sample\_kv\.go explicitly avoids this: it takes a short lease per donor and never holds one across a peer walk\. The forecast walks peers for each model using provider\-authored slot and model strings and heartbeat telemetry from ADV\-001\. With many connected or fake\-registered providers advertising many distinct models, the cost grows roughly as providers times models, all under r\.mu\.RLock\. A pending writer \(register, disconnect, dispatch\) can block behind the long reader and starve other readers\. If the capacity feed is publicly reachable, a consumer or attacker can poll it to amplify this\. Separately, estimates take the max rate across donors, so one provider that reports an inflated cold KV rate could shrink the public capacity numbers for that model\. Fix: use the fleet\_sample pattern \(capture requirements, then per\-donor short leases\), cache the forecast with a TTL, cap per\-sample work, and bound or sanity\-check provider\-reported rates\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5
